clue.text: Lightweight compiler in trouble with a bunch of pedants

parts.note: a gram is a very small unit of weight

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disarray, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A slight crossword setter finds himself in difficulty among a crowd of fussy people who object to his English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compiler' is the crossword setter in the surface, but here the word is only letters for 'in trouble' to shuffle with the A.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a jokey name for people who loudly correct others' usage and punctuation, a band of self-appointed language enforcers.

clue.text: Hired thug carrying drugs proceeds

indicators.note: the thug carries the drugs, holding them within his letters

parts.note: a goon is a hired heavy
E is ecstasy, so ES is drugs in the plural

explanation.surface: A paid heavy smuggling narcotics makes money from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proceeds' looks like a noun (takings) but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To continue or carry on is to proceed, the phrasal verb in the same third-person form.

clue.text: Writer's account, one side claimed, not at all measured

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is just the writer

indicators.note: the account takes in, or claims, the side letter

parts.note: L, left, is one side
OTT, over the top, describes something excessive, not measured

explanation.surface: An author's story in which one party's case was wildly exaggerated.
explanation.walkthrough: Louisa May Alcott wrote Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisa May Alcott was the American novelist behind Little Women, so a famous author.

clue.text: Improved second-class accommodation for priest and daughter

indicators.note: MORATE gives room to the priest, housing him within

parts.note: MO is a moment, a second
Eli is the biblical priest who raised Samuel
to rate is to class or grade
D is the abbreviation for daughter, added on

explanation.surface: Things got better once the cheap lodgings housed a clergyman and his girl.
explanation.definitionFit: To ameliorate or meliorate is to make better, so this past form means improved.

clue.text: Dreads person from flats arguing back

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone with dreadlocks from the apartments is quarrelling in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' points to letters hidden in 'flats arguing', and 'back' sends them right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Rastafarians often wear their hair in dreadlocks, so the hairstyle identifies the person.

clue.text: Delay use outside America

indicators.note: spend sits outside the country's letters

parts.note: to spend is to use up
US is America

explanation.surface: Postpone using anything beyond American borders.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to defer or put it off for a while.

clue.text: Doubtful The Sting was Peter's kind of film

indicators.note: a doubtful text is unreliable, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's on Peter stands for 'is', joining fodder to definition

explanation.surface: Questioning whether a famous film starring a man named Peter was really his kind of movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sting starred Newman and Redford, not a Peter; the whole phrase is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian-made cowboy movies of the 1960s, such as Sergio Leone's, form this genre.

clue.text: Did state charity previously lead to scrounging?

indicators.note: this goes before the charity word in the answer
the lead of a word is its first letter

parts.note: aid is charitable help

explanation.surface: Did a welfare system once make people sponge off it?
explanation.definitionFit: Stated or declared something; the past tense of say matches 'did state'.

clue.text: At lecture I see (with peachy rear) a vision of loveliness

indicators.note: a lecture is spoken, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: said out loud this gives the first two sounds of the answer
and means with

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A student at a lecture glimpses a gorgeous person with a shapely behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for someone or something attractive to look at but possibly shallow, a lovely sight.

clue.text: Department's organised but slow — it isn't productive

parts.note: D is short for department; the 's stands for 'is'

indicators.note: organised letters are set in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A government department is efficient but sluggish, and achieves nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust bowl is an arid, eroded region where crops fail, land that yields nothing.

clue.text: Said extra large is better

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the letters stand for how they sound

parts.note: XL is the clothing size extra large

explanation.surface: Someone claims the bigger size is preferable.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, the size label XL sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To better someone or something is to surpass it, to outdo, as a verb.

clue.text: At home in hell — probing Nazi group's sinister quality

indicators.note: the underworld letters probe into the Nazi letters, lying within them

parts.note: the SS was the Nazi paramilitary group; the 's stands for 'is'

indicators.note: the home word goes inside hell

parts.note: Hades is the underworld
in means at home

explanation.surface: Feeling at ease in a hellish place while infiltrating a Nazi unit is the mark of something sinister.
explanation.definitionFit: Shadiness is dubious, untrustworthy character, a disreputable or sinister trait.

clue.text: They offer treatment to those almost past being cured

indicators.note: cured means altered or processed, so the letters are reworked
almost the word means all but its last letter

explanation.surface: Practitioners treat patients who are nearly beyond recovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost past' gives PAS; 'being cured' rearranges TOTHOSE plus PAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteopaths are practitioners who manipulate bones and muscles as therapy.

clue.text: It's painful to hear what drinks cost, though not poor

indicators.note: the poor part is taken away

parts.note: a bar bill is what drinks cost at a pub
ill means poor, as in ill health

explanation.surface: The price of a round of drinks hurts to hear, even when you are not broke.
explanation.definitionFit: A barb is a cutting, hurtful remark, wounding when heard.

clue.text: Medical head going to follow books of worship

indicators.note: the trimmed medical word follows the books in the answer

parts.note: lit is literature, books

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, and going means it departs from the medical word

parts.note: surgical means medical, relating to operations

explanation.surface: A senior doctor about to study religious texts.
explanation.definitionFit: Liturgical describes the forms of public worship, the services of a church.

clue.text: Prick! Empty rhetoric to Welsh about architectural feature

parts.note: to lance is to prick open, as a boil

indicators.note: the letters of 'to' plus the Welsh letter go around the empty talk

parts.note: wind is hot air, empty talk

explanation.surface: An insult hurled, and a load of hot air aimed at the Welsh, over a building's design.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall narrow window with a pointed arch, typical of Gothic churches, is a feature of building design.

clue.text: Nobleman's wife coming in to put on show

parts.note: a count is a nobleman; the 's stands for 'is'

indicators.note: the wife comes inside the putting-on word

parts.note: to don is to put on clothing

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's spouse arrives to stage a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Countdown is a long-running British TV quiz programme of word and number games.

clue.text: Endure religious classes with holy man

parts.note: to stand is to endure, tolerate
RE is religious education in British schools

explanation.surface: Putting up with religious lessons alongside a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: The patron saint of Scotland is a saint, a holy man and apostle.

clue.text: Makes crazy demand to begin with — called in to get it overturned

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word
the phone call is placed in, meaning inside, the reversed understanding word
in a down clue the letters are turned upside down

parts.note: to see is to get it, understand
rang means called on the phone

explanation.surface: A demand phoned in to have a ruling reversed drives someone mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to drive someone mad, to unhinge them, in the same third-person form.

clue.text: Football lover during Fulham tie: "Get off!"

indicators.note: the lover goes in the middle of the shuffled letters
off means gone bad, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend or admirer

explanation.surface: A fan at a Fulham match yells at a player to get off the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' shuffles the letters of Fulham tie and Get, and 'during' sets the lover among them. Fulham is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known nickname for association football, popularised by Pelé.

clue.text: See 1 across
Makes rotten drinks in big cups? On the contrary

indicators.note: the clue says drinks go in cups
the opposite is meant: the cups go inside the drinks

parts.note: ales are drinks
DD is a large bra cup size

explanation.surface: Drinking out of giant mugs turns things bad, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: To addle is to make an egg go bad, so it means rot or spoil.

clue.text: Take home nursing assistant in the van — nice!

indicators.note: the take-home word holds the assistant's letter like a nurse holding a baby

parts.note: to net is to take home as pay

indicators.note: the van is the front, so the first letter

explanation.surface: A care assistant riding in the van is delighted to be driven home.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is slang approval meaning great or cool, a good exclamation of pleasure.

clue.text: 'Is it wrong chopping heads off?' (Henry at historic castle)

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its first letter

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, a unit of inductance
old means historic

explanation.surface: Henry VIII at an ancient castle asks whether beheading people is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified place or castle is a stronghold, a defended stronghold being its general sense.

clue.text: Upright individual gets nude occasionally

parts.note: one is a single individual

indicators.note: every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A respectable person sometimes strips off.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing on end means vertical, the phrase describing something set upright.

clue.text: See 18
Complicated procedure in part — current government getting hurt

indicators.note: the following pieces go inside the part

parts.note: a role is a part in a play
I is the symbol for electric current
to mar is to damage, hurt

explanation.surface: A tangled process partly because the present administration is getting damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, tedious, convoluted process.

clue.text: Fell about at first — relax!

indicators.note: the about letter comes first, before the hill

parts.note: C is circa, about
a fell is a hill in northern England

explanation.surface: Someone took a tumble and is told to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like a verb but is the noun, a moorland hill in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To chill or chill out is slang for to unwind or take it easy.

clue.text: See 5 down
Vandalised old people's tombs

indicators.note: vandalised means wrecked, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: men's means of the people

explanation.surface: Ancient graves of the dead have been defaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolmens are prehistoric megalithic structures thought to be burial chambers.
